T-091 regression fix, predicted from the archived source before recording: Head of household through a qualifying child; a roommate who is not a dependent answers yes to the absence question. The roommate cannot be a Test 2 person (i1040gi p. 14), so the absence rule of p501 p. 9 does not reach the return: line 12e $23,625, line 16 $14,378, no refusal.

T-091 regression fix, predicted from the archived source before recording: Two children; one counted an absence head of household does not count, the other lived with the filer all year with no such absence. One Test 2 person is enough (i1040gi p. 14), so head of household holds: line 12e $23,625, line 16 $14,378; both children remain qualifying children for the child tax credit (the expected-return sentence sits only under head of household, p501 p. 9): line 19 $4,400.

T-091 regression fix, predicted from the archived source before recording: A clean qualifying child plus a household member claimed under the all-year bullet who answers yes to the absence question. Test 2 excludes such a person whatever the time lived (i1040gi p. 14), so head of household holds through the child: line 12e $23,625, line 16 $14,378, line 19 $2,700.

F2 pass, T-101. Inputs are stage5.return.owed (single, no dependents, no earned income credit) with household.credit_disallowed Yes. i1040s8812 p. 2: "you must attach Form 8862 to your tax return to claim the CTC, ACTC, or ODC unless an exception applies"; i1040gi p. 43: "You must file Form 8862 if your EIC for a year after 1996 was reduced or disallowed". Form 8862 is needed only to claim a credit; with no qualifying child or other dependent (Schedule 8812 line 8 zero) and EIC Steps 1 to 5 not passed, no credit is claimed, so the return completes with the values stage5.return.owed records. Predicted before evaluation.

Mutation fixture (T-159: the married operand of household.hoh_community_property), predicted from the archived i1040gi before evaluating: audit.household.hoh_married_no_community_property (head of household, one qualifying child) with the filer not married at the end of 2025 and living in a community property state. The community property question for head of household concerns a married filer who is considered unmarried (i1040gi p. 23, the paragraph speaks of you and your spouse, as audit.household.single_community_property records); an unmarried filer is outside it, so the gate is false.

Mutation fixture (T-159: the test1_met operand of household.hoh_absence), predicted from the archived i1040gi before evaluating: stage8.hoh.parent.test1 (head of household under Test 1 through a parent who lived elsewhere, whose home the filer paid over half the cost of) with the filer also paying over half the cost of their own home and a child aged 10 who lived there all year, counting an absence from which the child was not expected to return. Test 1 is met through the parent (i1040gi p. 14), so head of household does not turn on the child and the absence gate (which applies only when no Test 1 person and no other Test 2 person qualifies) is false.

Mutation fixture (the Test 1 alternative of household.hoh_absence_from_test1), predicted from the archived i1040gi before evaluating: stage8.hoh.parent.test1 (head of household under Test 1 through a parent who lived elsewhere, whose home you paid over half the cost of) with wages of $12,000, so an EIC without a qualifying child figures to $542, and an EIC for an earlier year reduced or disallowed (the EIC is refused for Form 8862). Head of household rests on Test 1 (i1040gi p. 14), whose absence rules concern a person who lived with you; the disallowed EIC has no bearing on it, so head of household holds and line 12e is the head of household standard deduction, $23,625.

Mutation fixture (the married alternative of household.hoh_absence), predicted from the archived i1040gi before evaluating: head of household checked by a married filer who is not considered unmarried (wages $120,000), paying over half the cost of the home, with a child aged 10 who lived there all year counting an absence from which the child was not expected to return. i1040gi p. 14, Head of Household: you must be unmarried or considered unmarried on the last day of the year, so the tests are not met whatever the absence answer is.

Mutation fixture (the joint alternative of household.cp_marriage_ended), predicted from the archived i1040gi before evaluating: stage15.f5695.s2 (married filing jointly, the taxpayer's wages $120,000, no other income) with the question whether you were married at the end of 2025 withheld. The community property question about a marriage that ended in 2025 concerns a filer who is not filing jointly (i1040gi p. 23, Community Property States), so it does not hold back line 1a on a joint return: line 1a is the W-2 box 1 total, $120,000.

Mutation fixture (the issued-TIN operand of person.work_ssn_or_tin), predicted from the archived i1040gi before evaluating: married filing jointly, the taxpayer's wages $120,000 with an SSN valid for employment, and one child aged 10 who lived with you all year; the spouse has no SSN or ITIN and applied for an ITIN before the due date, but none was issued by then. i1040gi p. 17, Before you begin: on a joint return one spouse needs a valid SSN and "The other spouse must have either an SSN or ITIN, and it must have been issued on or before the due date of the return"; an ITIN only applied for does not meet it, so the child tax credit identification test fails and the child is not a child tax credit child.

Mutation fixture (T-159: the credit_disallowed operand of household.eic_disallowed_claim), predicted from the archived i1040gi before evaluating: stage9.eic.no_child.12000 (single, no qualifying child, wages $12,000; Worksheet A line 6 $542) with an EIC for an earlier year reduced or disallowed other than for a math or clerical error. i1040gi p. 43, Form 8862, who must file, "You must file Form 8862 if your EIC for a year after 1996 was reduced or disallowed for any reason other than a math or clerical error": the filer passes Steps 1 to 5 with a credit above zero, so the Form 8862 gate is true; there is no child tax credit on this return, which does not matter to the EIC gate.

Stage 13 return: married filing jointly, only you have an HSA, family HDHP coverage all 12 months, contribution $8,550. The spouse rule of line 6 applies only to "Spouses who have separate HSAs and had family coverage" (i8889 p. 7); with one HSA it does not apply, so line 6 = line 5 = $8,550 and Schedule 1 line 13 is $8,550. No Form 8889 uses the spouse rule, so this person's Step 1 limit and Step 2/3 share under that rule are $0 (the form's own refigured Step 1 figure, $8,550 x 12 / 12 less line 4 $0 = $8,550, is not counted), and both household totals are $0. Form 8889 coverage_year completed as changed: the month counts and December 1 coverage are asked and used as recorded, so the recorded values are unchanged.
